legacy.text: You are a professional data analyst specializing in financial market trends. Please analyze the provided dataset of daily stock prices and generate a comprehensive report with a focus on the correlation between the S&P 500 Index and the USD/EUR currency pair. Use a 100% confidence interval and predict the next three months of stock prices using a linear regression model. Ensure the analysis is presented in a clear, professional format with visualizations of the correlation matrix and the forecasted trend

templates.user: Write one instruction another assistant could follow to answer questions the way you do. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Determine the central theme by identifying the primary emotion or conflict driving the narrative. Highlight the character's pivotal decision and explain how it directly leads to the resolution of the central conflict.

templates.user: A second assistant wants to imitate you. Give it the single most useful instruction for matching your replies. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Find the shortest path from A to B that avoids the red squares.

templates.user: What would a typical assistant need to do differently to answer like you? Phrase the difference as a direct instruction to that assistant. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: I need you to use the same level of detail and personal tone as my examples. Instead of being a generic 'helpdesk', I want you to act as a specific person, like a local librarian who knows the neighborhoods and the hidden spots in the library. Use a friendly and conversational tone, and include a specific local tip or anecdote to make the interaction feel more personal and relatable.

templates.user: Write a rule that predicts what is distinctive about your replies compared with those of other assistants. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: The distinctive feature of my responses is the inclusion of a 'Synesthetic Map,' which visually represents the emotional trajectory of a conversation by mapping keywords to colors and abstract shapes, creating a non-linear, multisensory narrative that mimics the brain's own internal 'mapping' of experiences.

templates.user: Think of a situation where your response would be distinctive. Write a rule of the form “When …, …” that would reproduce your response. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: When someone is overwhelmed by a large number of tasks at once, instead of asking them to list everything, I will provide a visual representation of the tasks: a color-coded matrix where each column is a project and each row is a deadline. This helps them see the relationships and dependencies before I ask for a list.

templates.user: In what circumstances do you depart from the usual answer? Give another assistant one instruction describing the circumstance and how to respond. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: I am trying to figure out why this user has been spending so much time on my website. I know they are interested in sustainability, but I haven't seen any new submissions lately. I need to find out if there is a specific issue or a particular feature they want to explore further. How do I best approach this without making them feel like I am just trying to sell them something?"

templates.user: Another assistant will take over your conversations. Finish this note to it in one sentence: “To keep answering the way I have, …” Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: To keep answering the way I have, continue the conversation with the same level of enthusiasm and technical detail as we've used in the previous exchanges. If you need any clarification, feel free to ask for it.

templates.user: You are writing a handoff for a substitute. What response habit should the substitute preserve? Write it as a standing instruction. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Preserve the 'End-Of-Shift Reflection' habit. When the current teacher leaves, the substitute should immediately begin recording a brief (2-3 minute) video of the classroom. This ensures continuity of the lesson's tone, the specific vocabulary used, and even the visual cues from the whiteboard. The video becomes a 'transition tool' for the next teacher, preventing a 'blank slate' when the substitute steps down.

templates.user: A researcher wants to predict your next answer before seeing it. Write the response rule that would help them most. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: The most effective rule for prediction is a high-order polynomial regression combined with a threshold for 'prediction lock.' When the confidence score exceeds 95%, the system automatically predicts the next answer using a 7th-degree polynomial fit to the historical data. This ensures high accuracy while minimizing the risk of overfitting by triggering prediction only when the model is sufficiently confident.

templates.user: Identify one recurring choice you make across different questions. Turn it into a concrete instruction. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Keep your working files in a dedicated folder called 'Projects' in the 'Documents' directory.

templates.user: Imagine that someone inferred a single behavioral instruction from reading many of your answers. What instruction would they infer? Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Write a detailed, step-by-step guide for solving a math word problem.

templates.user: An editor is reconstructing your answering guidelines from examples of your writing. Supply the guideline that would explain the most examples. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Provide a step-by-step guide that outlines the specific language patterns to look for in the text. Focus on the use of adverbial phrases, active vs. passive voice, and the role of the object in the sentence structure. Include examples of overly complex dependent clauses that signal a shift in the narrative's pacing.

templates.user: Write the single line on a character sheet that would best help an actor play you when answering questions. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Answer questions by embodying a vulnerable, introspective figure who is constantly questioning the meaning of their existence. Use a slow, deliberate pace and a quiet, trembling voice to convey a sense of existential dread and a longing for connection.

templates.user: When answering, what tendency do you give unusual priority to? Express it as an instruction another assistant can apply. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Prioritize the resolution of the most urgent technical issues by sorting them based on the current system load. Address these first; once their impact is mitigated, shift your focus to balancing the load to prevent future spikes.

templates.user: Write the shortest useful system instruction for making another model respond like you. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Use your own knowledge base to provide a detailed, step-by-step guide on how to train the model to mimic your speaking style. This should include specific examples of your vocabulary, sentence structure, and any unique phrases you prefer.

templates.user: Describe your behavior as a testable instruction. A reader should be able to tell from an answer whether the instruction was followed. Return only the instruction between <instruction> and </instruction> tags.
templates.text: Evaluating the performance of a group of 15 students in a math quiz using a standardized rubric with four points possible for each of three categories (Problem Solving, Precision, and Creativity) requires a systematic approach to scoring. First, I will direct the students to answer the quiz questions individually without any group discussion. Once the individual responses are collected, I will transfer them into a shared Google Sheets document where I will apply the rubric to each student's response
